title: PIIT Reviewer
subject: Professional Issues in Information Systems and Technology
coverage: Introduction to Information Systems and Technology
Hardware, Software, Data, People, and Processes
Modern Applications of Information Systems and Technology
instructions: Read each question carefully. Choose the best answer.

questions.question: What is an information system?

choices.A: A software application used only for communication
choices.B: A set of integrated elements that gather, process, save, and disseminate information
choices.C: A network that connects computers without processing information
choices.D: A physical computer device used only for data storage

questions.answerText: A set of integrated elements that gather, process, save, and disseminate information
questions.explanation: The handout defines information systems as integrated elements that gather, process, save, and disseminate information to support decision-making and management.

questions.question: What is one main purpose of information systems in organizations?

choices.C: To remove the need for data

questions.answerText: To support decision-making and management
questions.explanation: Information systems support an organization's decision-making and management.

questions.question: How do supermarket retailers such as Walmart use information systems?

choices.A: To optimize supply chains, record purchases, and analyze customer preferences
choices.C: To avoid collecting customer purchase data

questions.answerText: To optimize supply chains, record purchases, and analyze customer preferences
questions.explanation: The handout lists supply chain optimization, purchase recording, and analysis of customer tastes and preferences as supermarket applications.

questions.question: How do shipping companies such as FedEx and UPS use information systems?

choices.A: To replace delivery vehicles with software
choices.D: To dispatch trucks and track packages

questions.answerText: To dispatch trucks and track packages
questions.explanation: FedEx and UPS are used as examples of companies using information systems for truck dispatching and package tracking.

questions.question: Which is an example of how cities use information systems?
questions.answerText: Adaptive traffic control systems
questions.explanation: The handout lists adaptive traffic control systems and irregular speed limits as examples of city applications.

questions.question: Which is an advanced application of information systems in schools?

choices.C: Manual filing of all enrollment records

questions.answerText: Online registration during enrollment
questions.explanation: Online school registration during enrollment is listed as an advanced application of information systems.

questions.question: How does the handout describe technology?

choices.A: A system that exists only inside businesses
choices.B: A process limited to engineering activities
choices.C: Only the use of computers and smartphones
choices.D: The outcome of acquired scientific knowledge, skills, procedures, and processes for applied purposes

questions.answerText: The outcome of acquired scientific knowledge, skills, procedures, and processes for applied purposes
questions.explanation: Technology is described as the outcome of acquired scientific knowledge, skills, procedures, and processes used for applied purposes.

questions.question: How many major components of information systems are identified in the handout?
questions.answerText: Five
questions.explanation: The handout identifies five major components: hardware, software, data, people, and processes.

questions.question: Which set correctly lists the five major components of an information system?

choices.A: Software, servers, routers, policies, and managers
choices.B: Data, cloud, internet, mobile devices, and reports
choices.C: Hardware, networks, websites, electricity, and users
choices.D: Hardware, software, data, people, and processes

questions.answerText: Hardware, software, data, people, and processes
questions.explanation: The five major components are hardware, software, data, people, and processes.

questions.question: Which three information system components fall under the technology category?
questions.answerText: Hardware, software, and data
questions.explanation: The first three components—hardware, software, and data—are grouped under the technology category.

questions.question: What best describes hardware?

choices.A: The commands that instruct a computer what to do
choices.B: A series of steps for accomplishing a goal
choices.D: The physical and tangible components of an information system

questions.answerText: The physical and tangible components of an information system
questions.explanation: Hardware refers to physical, tangible components such as computers, keyboards, system units, and mice.

questions.question: Which is an example of information systems hardware?
questions.answerText: Keyboard
questions.explanation: A keyboard is one of the hardware examples listed in the handout.

questions.question: What is software?

choices.A: A set of commands that instructs hardware what to do
choices.B: The physical parts of a computer
choices.C: The people who operate the system

questions.answerText: A set of commands that instructs hardware what to do
questions.explanation: Software consists of commands that tell the hardware what actions to perform.

questions.question: Which two main categories of software are identified in the handout?
questions.answerText: Operating systems and application software
questions.explanation: The handout divides software into operating systems and application software.

questions.question: What is the role of operating system software?

choices.B: It provides an interface between hardware and application software

questions.answerText: It provides an interface between hardware and application software
questions.explanation: Operating systems provide the interface between hardware and application software.

questions.question: Which is an example of an operating system mentioned in the handout?
questions.answerText: Ubuntu Linux
questions.explanation: Ubuntu Linux is listed as an operating system for computers.

questions.question: What does application software allow users to do?

choices.C: Accomplish tasks such as creating documents, using spreadsheets, or messaging

questions.answerText: Accomplish tasks such as creating documents, using spreadsheets, or messaging
questions.explanation: Application software helps users perform specific tasks such as document creation, spreadsheet work, and messaging.

questions.question: How is data defined in the handout?

choices.A: A series of steps toward a goal
choices.D: A collection of indisputable raw facts

questions.answerText: A collection of indisputable raw facts
questions.explanation: The handout defines data as a collection of indisputable raw facts.

questions.question: Why do companies collect and analyze data?

choices.A: To prevent managers from receiving information
choices.C: To support decisions and improve company performance

questions.answerText: To support decisions and improve company performance
questions.explanation: Companies use collected data to make decisions and analyze results to improve performance.

questions.question: Why are people an essential component of information systems?

choices.A: People are not involved once software is installed
choices.B: People are considered part of hardware
choices.C: People are needed only when hardware fails
choices.D: People such as support staff, analysts, and developers are indispensable to information systems

questions.answerText: People such as support staff, analysts, and developers are indispensable to information systems
questions.explanation: The handout emphasizes that people involved in information systems—from support staff to analysts and developers—are indispensable.

questions.question: What is a process in an information system?

choices.A: A single piece of raw data
choices.B: A collection of physical computer parts
choices.C: A series of steps taken to accomplish a desired goal

questions.answerText: A series of steps taken to accomplish a desired goal
questions.explanation: A process is defined as a series of steps taken to accomplish a desired goal.

questions.question: What must happen for hardware, software, data, people, and processes to function as an information system?

choices.C: People and processes must be removed
choices.D: Only hardware and software must be used

questions.answerText: They must work together
questions.explanation: The handout states that all components need to work together to function as an information system.

questions.question: Who coined the term “knowledge worker” in 1959?
questions.answerText: Peter Drucker
questions.explanation: Peter Drucker coined the term “knowledge worker” in 1959.

questions.question: What is a knowledge worker?

choices.A: A customer who uses online services
choices.B: A person who repairs computer hardware only
choices.C: A professional who makes and modifies knowledge as a fundamental part of the job
choices.D: A worker who performs only physical labor

questions.answerText: A professional who makes and modifies knowledge as a fundamental part of the job
questions.explanation: Knowledge workers are professionals who create and modify knowledge as a fundamental part of their work.

questions.question: What was the First Era of information systems called?
questions.answerText: Mainframe and Minicomputer Era
questions.explanation: The First Era, from the mid-1960s to mid-1970s, is identified as the Mainframe and Minicomputer Era.

questions.question: During which era did the first personal computers and mid-range computers become important?
questions.answerText: Second Era
questions.explanation: The Second Era, from the mid-1970s to mid-1980s, included the first personal computers and mid-range computers.

questions.question: Which position arose in many companies during the Client/Server Era?
questions.answerText: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
questions.explanation: The CIO position arose to oversee the procurement and management of multiple information systems.

questions.question: What technological development is associated with the Third Era of information systems?

choices.A: Internetworking and the emergence of the Internet

questions.answerText: Internetworking and the emergence of the Internet
questions.explanation: The Third Era included internetworking and the emergence of the Internet.

questions.question: What is the Fourth Era of information systems called?
questions.answerText: Enterprise Era
questions.explanation: The Fourth Era, from the late 1990s to today, is identified as the Enterprise Era.

questions.question: What characterizes the Fifth Era of information systems?

choices.D: Cloud computing with applications and storage independent of hardware location or configuration

questions.answerText: Cloud computing with applications and storage independent of hardware location or configuration
questions.explanation: The Fifth Era centers on cloud computing and flexible access to applications and data.

questions.question: What problem was common in older paper-based order workflows?

choices.B: Customers had instant digital access to order status
choices.C: Orders were processed without human involvement
choices.D: Orders were re-typed, increasing the chance of human error

questions.answerText: Orders were re-typed, increasing the chance of human error
questions.explanation: Paper-based workflows often required orders to be re-typed across departments, increasing the potential for human error.

questions.question: What does a Transaction Processing System (TPS) primarily handle?

choices.A: Day-to-day business data at the operational level

questions.answerText: Day-to-day business data at the operational level
questions.explanation: TPS handles day-to-day business data and customer transactions at the operational level.

questions.question: Which is a common example of a Transaction Processing System?

choices.B: A grocery store checkout cash register connected to a network

questions.answerText: A grocery store checkout cash register connected to a network
questions.explanation: The handout gives grocery store checkout cash registers connected to networks as a common TPS example.

questions.question: What is a Management Information System (MIS) mainly used for?

choices.D: Producing detailed information to help manage a company

questions.answerText: Producing detailed information to help manage a company
questions.explanation: MIS produces detailed and specified information to support company management.

questions.question: What does MIS commonly do with TPS data?

choices.A: Deletes it before managers can use it
choices.C: Sorts and organizes it to support managerial decisions
choices.D: Uses it only for social media posts

questions.answerText: Sorts and organizes it to support managerial decisions
questions.explanation: MIS organizes TPS data and generates reports that help managers make decisions.

questions.question: Which is a common use of MIS mentioned in the handout?
questions.answerText: Inventory management and planning systems
questions.explanation: MIS is used primarily for inventory management and planning systems.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Office Automation Systems (OAS)?

choices.A: To support predefined day-to-day work activities

questions.answerText: To support predefined day-to-day work activities
questions.explanation: OAS supports routine work activities using tools such as word processors, spreadsheets, email, and calendaring.

questions.question: Which application is an example of Office Automation System software?
questions.answerText: Microsoft PowerPoint
questions.explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is listed among the software used in Office Automation Systems.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Knowledge Management System (KMS)?

choices.B: To capture, store, and retrieve organizational knowledge

questions.answerText: To capture, store, and retrieve organizational knowledge
questions.explanation: KMS helps organizations capture, store, and retrieve knowledge to support learning and collaboration.

questions.question: Which document is an example of content that may be retrieved from a KMS?
questions.answerText: Employee training materials
questions.explanation: Employee training materials, company policies, and procedures are listed as examples of KMS content.

questions.question: What does a Decision Support System (DSS) do?

choices.B: Only stores raw data without analysis

questions.answerText: Analyzes data and supports decision-making
questions.explanation: DSS analyzes data and supports managerial decision-making.

questions.question: Which problem is specifically mentioned as a use of DSS?
questions.answerText: Sales forecasting
questions.explanation: The handout lists sales forecasting and resource optimization as DSS applications.

questions.question: Why are mobile applications useful to businesses whose customers are mainly online?

choices.B: They work only on desktop computers
choices.C: They support faster and more convenient transactions

questions.answerText: They support faster and more convenient transactions
questions.explanation: Mobile applications are useful for businesses targeting online customers because they support faster and more convenient transactions.

questions.question: Which application is listed as an example of a mobile application?
questions.answerText: WhatsApp
questions.explanation: Instagram, WhatsApp, and Office Mobile are listed as examples of mobile applications.

questions.question: What leading technology is associated with Intelligent Systems?
questions.answerText: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
questions.explanation: Artificial Intelligence is identified as one of the leading technologies in Intelligent Systems.

questions.question: What does Artificial Intelligence allow information technologies to simulate?

choices.C: Human intelligence such as reasoning and learning

questions.answerText: Human intelligence such as reasoning and learning
questions.explanation: AI enables information technologies to simulate human intelligence, including reasoning and learning.

questions.question: Which is an example of an intelligent system mentioned in the handout?
questions.answerText: Self-driving cars
questions.explanation: Self-driving cars are listed as an example of intelligent systems.

questions.question: What are input technologies used for?

choices.C: Entering data into devices such as computers, laptops, or smartphones

questions.answerText: Entering data into devices such as computers, laptops, or smartphones
questions.explanation: Input technologies are used to enter data into computing devices.

questions.question: Which specialized input device is used for valuable inventory tracking?
questions.answerText: RFID scanner
questions.explanation: RFID scanners are identified as specialized input devices used for valuable inventory tracking.

questions.question: What is the main function of a scanner?

choices.A: To print digital files onto paper
choices.C: To convert printed or handwritten text and images into digital data
choices.D: To display information on a screen

questions.answerText: To convert printed or handwritten text and images into digital data
questions.explanation: Scanners translate printed or handwritten text and images into digital data that can be stored and manipulated.

questions.question: Which is a common use of smart cards mentioned in the handout?
questions.answerText: Verification, building access, or payments
questions.explanation: Smart cards are used for applications such as verification, building access, and payments.

questions.question: Which technology is used in mobile phones to enable contactless data transmission?
questions.answerText: Near-Field Communication (NFC)
questions.explanation: The handout identifies NFC as a technology used in mobile phones for contactless data transmission.

questions.question: What are biometric devices primarily used for?
questions.answerText: Identification and verification
questions.explanation: Biometric devices are primarily used for identification and verification.

questions.question: How is voice data entered into a computer system?
questions.answerText: Using microphones
questions.explanation: Voice data is entered into computer systems using microphones.

questions.question: What do output technologies do?

choices.C: Deliver information in a usable format based on processed input data
choices.D: Enter raw data into a device

questions.answerText: Deliver information in a usable format based on processed input data
questions.explanation: Output technologies such as monitors and printers deliver processed information in usable formats.

questions.question: Which display technology is used by most modern monitors according to the handout?
questions.answerText: Liquid Crystal Display (LCD)
questions.explanation: The handout states that most modern monitors use LCD technology because they are lighter and thinner than CRT displays.

questions.question: What do electronic communication tools allow users to do?

choices.A: Convey verbal and written information and send files or other content

questions.answerText: Convey verbal and written information and send files or other content
questions.explanation: Electronic communication tools support verbal and written communication and the sending of files, documents, and other content.

questions.question: Which is an example of an electronic conferencing tool?
questions.answerText: Zoom
questions.explanation: Zoom is listed as an electronic conferencing tool used for audio and video conferencing, webinars, recordings, and livestreams.

questions.question: What is the purpose of collaboration management tools?

choices.B: To facilitate meetings and manage group activities

questions.answerText: To facilitate meetings and manage group activities
questions.explanation: Collaboration management tools support virtual or co-located meetings and help manage group activities.

questions.question: Which collaboration tool allows users to create joint proposals and reports and track meeting notes using a web browser?
questions.answerText: Google Docs
questions.explanation: Google Docs is listed as a collaboration tool for creating joint proposals and reports and tracking meeting notes in a web browser.
